<a id="migrations"></a>

# Migrations

`pecia migrate` covers the persisted formats a CLABOK book depends on: the manifest, the library registry, the container format, the open state, the ID ledger, the store marker, the project configuration and the derived book state. Migrations are forward-only and run on closed books.

`migrate plan` lists the ordered steps and the backup targets and writes nothing. `migrate apply` writes only with `--write`, and the global `--dry-run` always wins over it. `--to` sets a manifest target and refuses a downgrade with `migrate.downgrade`; `--strict` turns the first per-book warning into a failure.

`migrate status` reports the version and pending steps of every book and of the store metadata without writing anything. `--book` inspects one book; without a scope it reports every book. A missing registry is `registry-missing`, an unsupported version is reported with its target, and per-book errors are warnings, so one broken book does not hide the rest.

A book migration requires a closed book. It takes the store and the book lock, copies the container to `migrations/<timestamp>/<book>.book`, creates a rollback point with reason `migrate-v<from>-v<to>`, replaces only `manifest.json`, verifies IDs, regions, block metadata and body hashes, removes the derived `state.json`, and restores the container when anything fails. A receipt records every from and to version, every step, backup and warning. `--all` also migrates the registry, the store marker, the configuration and the transient open state, each with its own backup.

An authoring write on an older manifest is refused with `migrate.required` and names the migration command. Read-only commands and `book open`/`book close` keep working; close preserves an old manifest byte for byte when nothing was written. Older books therefore stay readable, and a migration is always an explicit decision.

`migrate cleanup` keeps the newest history entries, ten by default, and removes older `migrations/<timestamp>/` directories only with `--write`. The rollback pool is separate and keeps its own limits. A new format adds a step; current books are a no-op. The version moves with the scope that adds the format, and the release tag follows once the whole plan is green.
